arithmetic.question: Did training GPT-6 (Astra) on ~100k GPUs use about as much electricity as New York City uses in a week?

gpu_count.note: 'more than 100,000 GPUs' (OpenAI via Fortune; Brockman via Stratechery); GB200 NVL72 per Huang; Abilene bldg 1-2 = 100,800 GB200 (Epoch citing Crusoe)

kw_per_gpu_all_in.note: low = Crusoe 206 MW / 100,000; central = Epoch 232.67 MW / 100,000 (1,200 W x 1.82 x PUE ~1.065); high = Epoch peak facility 295 MW / 100,800. All assume near-peak draw; real average draw is likely lower.

training_days.note: Undisclosed. 90 days = Epoch's assumption; Epoch notes many frontier runs now exceed 100 days.

arithmetic.formula: energy_GWh = gpus x kW_per_gpu x days x 24 / 1e6 ; nyc_weeks = energy_GWh / (50,104 x 7 / 365)
arithmetic.verdict: Overstated by ~2x. Central estimate ~503 GWh = ~3.7 days (~0.52 week) of NYC electricity; plausible range ~2-6 days. Reaching a full NYC-week would need ~172 days of pretraining at ~233 MW, or ~137 days even at Epoch's peak facility power (~293 MW) - longer than any evidence suggests. Safe slide phrasing: 'Training GPT-6 Astra used roughly as much electricity as New York City uses in 3-4 days (Epoch-based estimate).'

facts.claim: Without data centers and information-processing investment, US GDP growth in H1 2025 would have been just 0.1% annualized; that ~4%-of-GDP category produced 92% of growth.
US spending on data centers and other information-processing hardware now exceeds housing (residential) investment.
AI-related data center construction, compute hardware and networking = ~0.8% of US GDP in Q1 2026; computing infrastructure overall ~1.5% of GDP, double the 2015-2022 average (~0.7%).
Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta are on track to spend ~$724B on capex in 2026 (up to $760B at guidance upper limits) and nearly $950B in 2027, vs $413B in 2025.
Hyperscaler capex (Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle) has grown ~72% per year since Q2 2023 - quadrupling since GPT-4 - reaching $448B in 2025.
Alphabet's free cash flow turned negative in Q2 2026 for the first time since its 2004 IPO after it raised 2026 capex to as much as $205B.
Nvidia became the first company worth $5 trillion (Oct 29, 2025) - more than the GDP of India, Japan or the UK; it is worth ~$5.65T as of Oct 3, 2026.
Nvidia's quarterly revenue doubled in a year to $96.2bn (+106%); Jensen Huang declared a “golden age”.
OpenAI's valuation went from $157B (Oct 2024) to $852B (Mar 2026), with talks at ~$1.4 trillion (Sep 2026); Anthropic raised $65B at a $965B valuation (May 2026).
Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate surged from $9B at end-2025 to over $65B by end of July 2026.
AI was the #1 stated reason for US layoffs for five straight months (Mar-Jul 2026); 116,175 AI-attributed cuts through August 2026, more than double all of 2025 (54,836).
In May 2026, 40% of all announced US job cuts (38,579) cited AI.
Block cut 4,000 of its 10,000 employees citing AI productivity - and its shares rose more than 20%.
Meta is expanding its Hyperion campus in Louisiana to 5 GW for more than $50 billion - up from a ~$10B price tag when construction began in 2024.

Microsoft's Fairwater (Wisconsin) AI datacenter: 315 acres, 1.2M sq ft, 46.6 miles of foundation piles, 26.5M lb of steel, 120 miles of medium-voltage cable; "10X the performance of the world’s fastest supercomputer today".
xAI's Colossus 2 in Memphis runs ~946 MW of IT power (~1.1M H100-equivalents, ~$36B) - powered partly by gas turbines placed across the state line in Mississippi.

Data centres used ~415 TWh (1.5% of world electricity) in 2024; IEA projects ~945 TWh by 2030 - more than Japan uses today. In the US, data centres account for nearly half of electricity demand growth to 2030.
US data centers used 4.4% of US electricity in 2023 (176 TWh, up from 58 TWh in 2014); projected 6.7%-12% (325-580 TWh) by 2028.
PJM capacity prices jumped from $28.92/MW-day (2024/25) to the $325-333 cap for three straight auctions; annual cost rose from $2.2B to $16.4B.
Without its price cap, PJM's 2028/29 auction would have cleared at ~$555/MW-day, and it still fell 6.8 GW short of its reliability requirement.
Texas has paused connecting new data centers to the grid to audit proposed projects, while US electricity sales hit record levels driven by data centers.
Conventional DRAM contract prices rose ~93-98% in a single quarter (1Q26), then another 58-63% in 2Q26; DRAM industry revenue nearly tripled from $53.6B (4Q25) to $154.7B (2Q26).
Micron and Samsung executives expect the memory shortage to last through 2028; memory for 2027 is priced "much higher than 2026 prices."
GE Vernova's gas turbine backlog + slot reservations grew from 100 GW to 116 GW in one quarter (Q2 2026), heading for at least 125 GW by year-end.
Power transformers are in a ~30% supply deficit; unit costs up 77% for power transformers and 78-95% for distribution transformers since 2019.
Over 2,060 GW of generation and storage (~8,200 projects; 1,312 GW of generation) was waiting in US grid interconnection queues at the end of 2025.
facts.source: LBNL Queued Up 2026 Edition (official page summary)

facts.claim: Local opposition blocked or delayed at least 75 US data center projects worth ~$130B in Q1 2026 - the most on record - and 45 more worth $68B in Q2.
About two-thirds of upcoming US datacenters are set to be built in places that have been among the driest in the country over the past year.
The US is building twice as much gas-fired capacity as China, largely to feed AI datacenters; under-construction gas projects up 76%.
US gas projects explicitly linked to data centers grew almost 25-fold in two years.
Google's total energy use jumped 36% in one year (32.3 TWh in 2024 to 44.0 TWh in 2025); its electricity demand is up >250% since 2019, freshwater use rose 37% in 2025, and emissions rose 18%.
A US regulator ruled xAI acted illegally by using dozens of methane gas turbines to power its Colossus datacenters in Tennessee.
"A shortage of electricity is the leading constraint on an otherwise roaring data center boom" - SpaceX committed $2.8B to buy gas turbines for its AI data centers.
US average residential electricity price: 16.5 cents/kWh (2024) to 17.3 (2025) to a projected 18.2 (2026) and 18.6 (2027).
Microsoft signed a 20-year deal to buy power from Three Mile Island Unit 1 - an 835 MW reactor shut in 2019 - so Constellation can restart it as the Crane Clean Energy Center.
facts.source: Microsoft Cloud Blog / Constellation press release

facts.claim: Financial terms of the Microsoft-Constellation 20-year agreement 'weren't disclosed'.
Crane restart was first targeted for 2028; Constellation now says it is 'ahead of schedule' and 'on track to return 835 megawatts ... to the grid in 2027'.
Constellation is spending $1.6 billion to restart the Crane reactor; DOE closed a $1 billion loan for it (announced Nov 18, 2025).

A PJM analysis suggested Crane might not connect to the grid until 2031; FERC then granted Constellation's waiver to move capacity interconnection rights from its Eddystone gas units to Crane, and the NRC approved Crane's fuel licence amendment.
facts.source: ANS Nuclear Newswire; Constellation Q2 2026 results (republished on StockTitan)

facts.claim: NRC issued its final environmental assessment and finding of no significant impact for the Crane restart (Federal Register, Sept 25, 2026); an exemption and three licence amendments are still pending.
A 262-ton transformer, shipped a month from South Korea, reached Three Mile Island on Aug 17, 2026, the first of three new power transformers for the restart.
Palisades (800 MW, shut May 2022) began loading fuel on Aug 30, 2026; a used fuel assembly tilted inside the reactor vessel and loading has been paused since. No restart date has been set.
facts.source: Holtec 'Progress Report on Palisades' March to Startup'; ANS; NEI Magazine

facts.claim: Holtec did not disclose the Aug 30 Palisades incident publicly until a Sept 21 progress report, about three weeks later; NRC says there was 'no radiological release'.
Palisades' restart targets have slipped from end-2025 to early 2026 and now to an open date; Holtec's contract calls for supplying power by March 2027.
Holtec postponed its planned $750M+ IPO in Sept 2026; its CEO blamed uncertainty about US data-center power demand.
Constellation shares fell 'from a high of over $400 last fall to the mid-$260s'; the VanEck Uranium and Nuclear ETF peaked above $160 in January and has lately traded below $110.
Google signed a 25-year deal to buy power from Iowa's Duane Arnold (615 MW, shut 2020); DOE closed a loan of up to $1.9B on Sept 8, 2026; restart targeted no later than Q1 2029.
DOE on Duane Arnold: 'Thanks to President Trump's Ratepayer Protection Pledge, hyperscalers, not taxpayers, are paying for the new power generation.'
Amazon will take up to 1,920 MW from Talen's Susquehanna nuclear plant through 2042, reaching full volume no later than 2032, alongside a $20B Pennsylvania data-center investment.

Amazon invested in X-energy (Oct 2024); its first project, with Energy Northwest in Washington, is four Xe-100 reactors (320 MW, expandable to 960 MW). The construction permit application is expected to be filed in the first half of 2027.
Google's Kairos deal covers up to 500 MW from six or seven small reactors, the first by 2030 and the rest by 2035; ground was broken on the 50 MW Hermes 2 in Oak Ridge on April 17, 2026.

Meta announced nuclear deals for up to 6.6 GW by 2035: more than 2.1 GW from two Vistra plants in Ohio plus 433 MW of uprates across three Vistra plants, up to eight TerraPower Natrium units (2.8 GW), and an Oklo campus of up to 1.2 GW in Ohio, to power its Prometheus supercluster.

Meta's first nuclear deal was a 20-year PPA for all 1,121 MW of Constellation's Clinton plant from June 2027, which keeps the plant running after Illinois' subsidy ends and adds 30 MW through uprates.
Amazon signed a 20-year, 690 MW PPA for Calvert Cliffs that includes a 190 MW uprate (online 2030-2032) and more than $3B of investment.
Google's first nuclear PPA outside the US is a 22-year deal for 50% of Finland's Loviisa plant over 2030-2049.
Constellation signed another 920 MW of 15-20 year nuclear PPAs in Q2 2026, including a 176 MW Walmart deal that enables a 30 MW uprate at Dresden.
OpenAI: GPT-6 Astra was 'the first time we've pretrained on more than 100,000 GPUs at our Stargate site in Texas' - the company's largest training run 'by far' (Aidan Clark, VP of research).
Greg Brockman: 'this is the first run that we've trained on more than 100,000 GPUs, which is an easy number to throw around, but just think about the scale of that.'
Jensen Huang (via X): Astra was trained on '~100K+ Nvidia Grace Blackwell NVLink72'; plans to bring 400,000 GPUs online next (4x).
OpenAI's EU AI Act summary: GPT-6 Astra 'is not a modification or a fine-tune of a prior model' and was trained on 'More than 10 trillion tokens'; placed on the EU market 3 September 2026.
facts.source: OpenAI, Public Summary of Training Content for GPT-6 Astra (v1, 2 Sep 2026)

facts.claim: Epoch AI estimates GPT-6 Astra at ~1e27 FLOP (90% CI ~5e26-2e27) - 'corresponding to ~100k GB200s over 90 days at 25% FP8 MFU' - about 50x GPT-4 (~2.1e25), drawing ~233 MW (232.67 MW) during training.
facts.source: Epoch AI 'Data on AI models' (all_ai_models.csv, row last modified 2026-09-23)

facts.claim: Epoch's power method: Training power draw = PUE x Server overhead (1.82, from DGX H100: 10.2 kW / 8 x 700 W) x Power per GPU x Hardware quantity; PUE 1.08 in 2025, declining ~0.8%/yr. For Astra this implies ~1,200 W per GB200 x 1.82 x ~1.065 = ~2.33 kW per GPU all-in.

Stargate Abilene (Crusoe): 1.2 GW of power capacity; eight buildings; 'Each building has been designed to operate up to 50,000 NVIDIA GB200 NVL72s'; 206 MW coming online in 2025; design PUE 'an average of 1.2 to 1.3'.
Larry Ellison: Abilene will house more than 450,000 Nvidia GB200 GPUs and 'will use 1.2GW, "enough power for one million four-bedroom homes in the United States"' - 'That's a pretty good-sized city.'

Epoch AI: Abilene buildings 1-2 (100,800 GB200) were fully operational by Dec 24, 2025 at ~211 MW IT / ~295 MW total facility power; the site is now ~421 MW IT (509k H100e, $15.9B) and projected at 843 MW IT / ~1.18 GW facility by Nov 2026. Oracle posted on Apr 22, 2026: 'In Abilene, 200MW is already operational'.
facts.source: Epoch AI data center directory (updated Oct 2, 2026)

facts.claim: A GB200 NVL72 rack (72 GPUs + 36 Grace CPUs) has a TDP of 132 kW nominal (peak electrical design ~192 kW) - ~1.83 kW per GPU before cooling and cluster networking.

SpaceX S-1: at Colossus II, xAI brought online ~110,000 GB200 processors = ~210 MW of compute power in 91 days, then 110,000 GB300 = 220 MW in 64 days; next phase adds at least 220,000 GB300 and over 400 MW. Colossus + Colossus II provide ~1.0 GW of compute power.
Epoch AI: xAI's Colossus 2 (Memphis) runs ~946 MW of IT power (~1.28 GW incl. cooling), ~1.11M H100-equivalents, $35.8B; projected 1,531 MW IT by Q1 2027.

Zuckerberg: 'We're calling the first one Prometheus and it's coming online in '26. We're also building Hyperion, which will be able to scale up to 5GW over several years.' Epoch now estimates Prometheus at 471 MW IT (~612 MW facility, Aug 2026); Hyperion's first phase ~1.6 GW IT (~2.2 GW facility) by 2028.
